speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat
text: asked the Minister for National Development (a) whether the Ministry will issue monthly guidelines for buyers and sellers of HDB flats under the Ethnic Integration Policy (EIP) on the pegging of the fair market value of these flats at a certain percentage of the last transacted price in the open category; and (b) in the past three years, what is the average discounted price of EIP flats transacted compared to prices in the open market.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan
text: asked the Minister for National Development whether HDB will consider introducing a policy akin to the Lease Buyback Scheme where HDB buys back flats belonging to non-Chinese flat owners when these owners are unable to sell their flats due to the Ethnic Integration Policy.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: It applies to the sale and purchase of all new and resale HDB flats and is implemented for all ethnic groups.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: The saleability of a flat in the open market is dependent on many factors and not just the EIP.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: While home owners may have their own expectations of how much their flat can sell for, flat attributes like location, storey height, physical condition of the flat, remaining lease and market sentiments would naturally be considered by prospective home buyers.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: To help home owners and buyers make an informed decision in their price negotiation, HDB provides daily updates of transacted prices of resale prices at the HDB InfoWEB.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: For those who are unable to sell their flats, HDB may grant them an extension of time and advise them to be realistic with their asking prices.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: HDB will continue to exercise flexibility for households with exceptional circumstances.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: I would just like to clarify that I fully support the EIP.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: But in relation to my question, why did HDB in the first instance have this extension option on a case-by-case basis?

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: The feeling is, is it not because it recognises the EIP, the market can be squeezed by the buyers in principle?

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: And the large number for appeals for extension, possibly, says something about the market.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: The second is: I have been seeing a lot of residents from the minority ethnic groups, they are unable to sell their flats.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: Not so much unable to sell their flats, but also the ability to sell their flats at a high price.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: So, it is usually squeezed to the extent that they are only able to sell their flats at a much lower price than the market.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: So, my worry is about whether this policy could potentially contribute to this squeeze actually worsening over time, and we are worsening the cycle for some of those involved in the EIP.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: In some instances, on the purchase side, it may help the buyer because the price may well be slightly lower; and on the flip side, of course, on the sales side, it sometimes may be more difficult.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: So, it really depends on the circumstance and on the nature of the transaction and for that particular location, which are the binding EIP limits.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: We put out data, information as far as possible to help facilitate the matching of demand and supply in the marketplace, and I think that is the right approach.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: But as I said earlier, we do monitor the situation carefully.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: We will extend assistance to those who need more time and we will continue to exercise flexibility for those who are in extenuating circumstances.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: The Minister said that when the buyer buys the flat, do they get a discount, especially if they buy from HDB?

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: Because my understanding is that they do not get a discount if they buy straight from HDB, but because of this EIP, it has squeezed demand for flats, and because of the squeeze on demand, the prices are affected.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: And prices come down, so why should the sellers be prejudiced because they are affected by the EIP in having to sell at a lower price, unless they are correspondingly given a discount when they first buy the flat, which is why I asked whether would HDB then step in to treat them as if this is a Lease Buyback Scheme.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: But in the resale market, when you make a purchase, the EIP can have an impact, just as when you make a sale decision, the EIP can have an impact.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: So, we will continue to monitor the system, make sure it works well, achieves the goals that we want it to achieve, and, where possible, continue to exercise flexibility in the way we administer the scheme.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat
text: Just a follow-up in relation to my question.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat
text: In the meantime, while we try to list some of the concerns of the residents that are having difficulties in selling, my suggestion is maybe by having a sharing of monthly guidelines for buyers and sellers in particular for the EIP scheme, will that in some way be a valuable suggestion in terms of the Ministry of National Development nudging buyers and sellers in that EIP locale to reduce the squeeze on the pricing of the units?

speaker: Mr Chong Kee Hiong (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: I see more of such cases in my Meet-the-People Sessions, especially in recent months.

speaker: Mr Chong Kee Hiong (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: HDB does give extension of time, but the common feedback is that despite extension of time, there are no viewers.

speaker: Mr Chong Kee Hiong (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: So, if there are no viewers, that means there is no offer at all.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: We really have to look at it case by case, because there are indeed instances where the residents have said they find it difficult.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: Can I clarify with the Minister if there are any statistics available on the number of minorities who own such HDB flats?

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: How much feedback has gone to HDB about their inability to sell their unit because of the EIP policy?

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: If Mr Pritam Singh would like to ask more in-depth questions on other data, we can easily follow up in a separate Parliamentary Question.
